# Additive capture v2: native refusal classification

Non-normative, unexecuted preparation by `/root/isometry_cli_tests`. Independent preexecution review found that frozen `capture_reversal.py` classifies every complete native error code as semantic refusal, including `limit` and `format`. That contradicts the distinctions stated in `scripts.md`. The original generator, capture, documentation, candidate, 84-file map and all original input files remain unchanged. No first or second script has been imported or executed by this author.

`capture_reversal_v2.py` is an additive copy of the frozen capture with four narrowly scoped changes: it guards the new complete capture input map before the original84 guard or local code import; it adds required explicit `--capture-design-map-sha256`; it excludes that additional capture hash from comparison against the original seven generation prerequisites; and it classifies complete native refusals accurately. The summary's scope text reflects the classification change. The original generator and its seven required hash arguments stay fixed as listed in `scripts.md`.

| Fully recorded native `error` code | V2 classification |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_ir` | `complete-native-semantic-refusal` |
| `contract` on inspection | `complete-native-semantic-refusal` |
| `contract` on the unchanged request | `predicted-native-contract-rejection-observed` |
| `limit` | `complete-native-capacity-refusal` |
| `format` | `complete-native-format-refusal` |
| Any other error code | `complete-unclassified-native-error` |

These classifications require complete actual native/client records, coherent return1, actual start/identity and matching raw API/kernel error protocol. Timeout, wrapper refusal, missing or malformed records, output caps, incomplete stdin, identity mismatch and incoherent return codes remain operational/incomplete observations. A malformed or unexpected response without those checks does not become a semantic result. Complete unrecognized outcomes and unexpected successes are preserved.

Only fully validated successful fresh inspection enables the request. Every refusal, capacity/format failure, unknown code, incomplete capture or unexpected inspect outcome skips it. At most two literal fixed client commands are possible; no retry, new request, source edit, fallback, matcher change or outcome-driven repair is performed.
